edits.new: The rules are data and library behaviour, not service code: BR2 is the two tables, BR3 is the change row and the ACE audit call, BR4 is the weekly Schedule, BR5 is the off-by-default rule of the interface, and BR6 is enforced by the naming library (DP-14), so a key that breaks the pattern never reaches the store. The flag tables sit in one platform-owned store whose schema name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1411) until RWB-PLT-DB allocates it; the library caches per service and the admin component is deployed with the rwb-integration platform route. The flag schemas are published from the legacy field identifiers DF-OPS-207 to DF-OPS-223 and the standard columns, and every POST carries an Idempotency-Key header while the PATCH carries If-Match with the version (AC8). The four flag paths are served by the platform library through gateway-bff, with P2 serving the admin API against it.
